A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProGVC research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-compression experiments, runtime measurements, qualitative reconstructions, and component ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports temporal-consistency results using t-LPIPS on Xiph in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same causal VAE, multi-scale residual quantization, sparse autoregressive context model, entropy coding, and generation of discarded tokens. Training objectives are unchanged. Token-level dropping is mentioned only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use filtered Pexels training data and evaluate on Xiph, HEVC B, MCL-JCV, and UVG, which already appears in v1's appendix. The new temporal metric uses existing Xiph coverage; the qualitative examples are exchanged between figures rather than added.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain VTM-17.0, DCVC-FM, DCVC-B, SEVC, and PLVC. Runtime and appendix comparisons retain their existing methods, including DiffVC, GNVC-VD, DVC, and DCVC. The new temporal-consistency table uses the existing main comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds t-LPIPS to the evaluation metrics and reports temporal-consistency BD-rate/BD-metric results on Xiph with VTM-17.0 as anchor. Existing training budgets, preprocessing, 720p/81-frame evaluation, bitrate configurations, and runtime hardware remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component and attention ablations in Section 4.3, intra-scale-dropping studies in Appendix C, and image-versus-video comparisons in Appendix D are retained. Qualitative cases are relocated. The added t-LPIPS table extends benchmark measurement without adding an ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed results, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run variability. Existing runtime averaging and sequence-level degradation proportions are retained; the new t-LPIPS results introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds Xiph t-LPIPS results: ProGVC achieves -20.76% BD-rate / 0.0007 BD-metric, compared with SEVC's -15.89% / 0.0004, and ranks best among the listed methods. Existing numerical results, plotted curves, runtimes, and ablation values are unchanged. Figures 5 and 8 exchange existing examples and their scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1-9 and the associated probability factorizations, quantization definitions, residual updates, and attention formulation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added; t-LPIPS is introduced as an evaluation metric without new mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about a visual-autoregressive progressive video codec unifying scalability, entropy coding, and detail synthesis. The new temporal-consistency evidence supports these contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds explanations linking temporal consistency to hierarchical generation and cross-frame attention, and stronger DISTS/NIQE performance than LPIPS to natural textures with local deviations. Section 5 further explains the computational difficulty of exceeding 720p and identifies token-level dropping as a future rate-control direction.

D1.justification: v1's runtime discussion explicitly identifies 50 diffusion steps for DiffVC; v2 omits that detail and the accompanying optimization remark. Hardware, implementation disclosures, training hyperparameters, and Appendix A's preprocessing and code-access information remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a change to the timing procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds a temporal-coherence reference for t-LPIPS and three references on machine-oriented compression: Video Coding for Machines, SMC++, and Free-VSC. A new introductory sentence distinguishes human viewing from machine analysis. The central positioning relative to generative codecs and visual autoregressive models is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the introduction, metric discussion, results interpretation, and future-work paragraph, while shortening the complexity discussion. Author ordering, affiliations, correspondence markers, and running headers also change. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the temporal-consistency table and rearranges existing experimental tables and figures. Figures 5 and 8 exchange ParkScene and videoSRC07 examples, with corresponding caption changes. Method diagrams are slightly resized, and spacing changes, while their visual content and existing plotted curves are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Xiph t-LPIPS comparison provides direct evidence about temporal consistency that v1 lacked. Added discussion of metric differences and the 720p limitation also improves interpretability. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the explicit DiffVC step-count detail; the method and broader empirical foundation remain unchanged.
